title: Detecting data and concept drift, and retraining

videos.script: It is the end of June. The lapse model has scored every night since February, and every night the watch said the same thing. Nothing out of line. {{quiet}} Meanwhile online orders stopped paying postage, and a book subscription opened in São Paulo. {{world}} The world a model learned from does not stay put. Sometimes the members change: what they look like, measured by the inputs. That is data drift, and it can be seen the same night. {{data}} Sometimes what the inputs mean changes: the same member, the same history, a different outcome. That is concept drift, and only the outcomes show it, ninety days late. {{concept}} This lesson finds both in four new months of the shop. A fixed reference that the nightly watch did not have. A report card that has finally arrived, and a split of it that says who changed. {{find}} Then the answer every monitoring system ends in. Train a challenger on newer data, through the same pipeline, and test it on the same night as the champion, by the rule lesson 3 set. {{retrain}} And one result the course does not hide. On the last day of June, no honest test can show that a retrained model has learned what changed in April. The labels have not caught up yet. {{honest}}
